insight.title: Why Having Fewer Options Helps You Move Faster
insight.subtitle: How removing a choice simplifies your day and reduces friction.

sections.text: When a project stalls, our instinct is to add: more people, more meetings, or more software. Yet, in complex systems, adding a new path usually creates more congestion than it actually clears.

In 1969, Stuttgart engineers closed a main road to fix traffic. Counterintuitively, flow improved immediately. They discovered that adding more options often slows a system down by creating too many competing decision points.
Most of your daily delays aren't caused by a lack of options, but by an abundance of them. True efficiency isn’t about having more ways to work; it is having fewer ways to hesitate.
Try this today: When you make a decision today, remove one valid option before choosing between the rest.
The strongest systems are defined by what they omit, not what they include.
